subject: Soft-burst window proposal and traffic-smoothing plan for Orchid Retail launch
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Orchid Retail <ops@orchidretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Orchid launch - soft-burst / smoothing asks and traffic projection attached

Markus / team —

Per our call this morning, Orchid is targeting a phased public launch Nov 17 with a heavy first-week push (marketing + influencer slots). They shared an early projection (attached) that shows a concentrated ingress spike: ~2.4M tokens/hour peak across their primary route for the first 48 hours, then settling to ~700k tokens/hour.

Two asks from commercial/sales:
- Can we offer a temporary "soft-burst" policy (short smoothing window) instead of a hard per-minute throttle so customer-side retries don't stack?
- If soft-burst isn't feasible, can we provide a time-limited quota uplift (days-weeks) and a recommended canary ramp schedule?

Operational notes we need from you (Grace / Aditya): expected SLO risks, monitoring requirements, and any immediate kernel/quantization impacts if we route to a cheaper variant under load.

I've attached orchid_launch_projection_v1.xlsx with per-route breakdowns. Orchid's ops is looped at ops@orchidretail.com — Maya is their launch lead.

Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Orchid Retail <ops@orchidretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid launch - soft-burst / smoothing asks and traffic projection attached

Thanks Karthik — read the projection. High level proposal below; want product + infra validation before committing to Orchid.

Proposal (internal summary):
- Soft-burst model: implement a 5-minute smoothing window for their primary generation route (averages token ingestion across window) with a short-term "leaky-bucket" allowance to absorb spikes. This reduces client retry amplification.
- Interim option: +25% temporary quota uplift (reserved capacity) for first 72 hours from launch, then step down 50% every 24h to baseline over 4 days.
- Canary ramp: start at 3% traffic, increase to 10% after 30m, 30% after 2h, full roll after 12h if no regressions.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model variant and auto-retry suppression header we can pass back to client.

Questions for Lauren (product): can soft-burst be exposed per-account via entitlements, or does it require runtime change? If the latter, how long to ship a configuration knob?

Grace / Aditya — can you validate the smoothing window idea operationally? Key asks: can we protect multi-tenant performance, instrument token-budget ledger, and add a temporary trace flag to keep detailed spans for the first 24h?

Orchid — tagging you so you're aware this is internal planning; Karthik will follow up with specifics we need to finalize.

-Markus
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Orchid Retail <ops@orchidretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid launch - soft-burst / smoothing asks and traffic projection attached

Quick product/roadmap response:

Short answer: hosted API does not currently support per-customer configurable smoothing windows out-of-the-box. We have two viable approaches today:
1) Entitlement-based temporary quota uplift (fast, ops-friendly). We can provision a reserved capacity slice and routing policy per-customer. Delivery: <48 hours with CS + billing sign-off.
2) Runtime change to expose a per-tenant smoothing/leaky-bucket window (native soft-burst). This is a product+runtime change; estimated 2 sprints (4 weeks) to spec, test, and roll to canary if prioritized.

If Orchid needs the soft-burst semantics specifically (not just more capacity), we can scope a targeted runtime knob scoped to the generation route. Acceptance criteria I'd need:
- Concrete percent of requests allowed above baseline in the 5-minute window
- Clear rollback thresholds (latency, error rate, memory pressure)
- Test plan including synthetic spike run and a canary group

For now I recommend option (1) + a short-term traffic-smoothing shim in the edge layer operated by infra (if possible) so we avoid shipping runtime changes under launch pressure.

I'll add JIRA-INF-2145 to track the runtime knob; if Sales wants us to prioritize, please update the ticket with customer commitment details.

-Lauren
Senior PM, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Orchid Retail <ops@orchidretail.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid launch - soft-burst / smoothing asks and traffic projection attached

Operational notes and runbook pointers:

- We can implement the smoothing at the ingress edge (rate window averaging) as a short-term mitigation. It won't be as precise as a kernel-level leaky-bucket but will reduce retry storms. Edge shim work estimate: 2-3 engineer-days and one canary region (us-west).
- Monitoring: enable detailed token-budget ledger for Orchid routes for 7 days (token counts per minute, tail latency buckets, 5xx/4xx by model variant). We'll keep trace sampling at 100% for first 12 hours, then 10% after stability.
- Suggested soft caps (ops recommendation): set a per-route cap at 3.0M tokens/hour with a soft allowance of +30% over any 5-minute window (enforced at edge). Pair with automated alert: 95th-percentile latency > 350ms or error rate > 1.5% -> immediate canary rollback.
- Caching note: encourage Orchid to enable prefix/KV cache on the primary route where possible to reduce token churn.

I've drafted runbook notes (runbook-soft-burst.md) and linked the Drive folder. If we go entitlement route, CS/Billing must approve the reserved capacity commit and appropriate billing terms.

-Grace
Head of Reliability Engineering

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@orchidretail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Orchid launch - soft-burst / smoothing asks and traffic projection attached

Thanks everyone — we appreciate the quick triage. We can accept a temporary quota uplift for the first 72 hours provided:
- Billing note appended to the contract (Karthik, can you confirm?)
- SLA exception for the initial 24h and an agreed rollback plan if performance degrades

We also prefer the soft-burst behavior (reduces client-side retry loops). If the product route to ship a runtime knob takes too long, the entitlement uplift + edge smoothing is acceptable. We'll confirm final traffic slots by EOD Nov 10.

Maya Singh
Senior Launch Manager, Orchid Retail
ops@orchidretail.com
